name: Spam Musubi — Hawaiian Spam Rice Block
subtitle: Hawaiian Spam Rice Block
description: Hawaii's convenience-store staple: Spam fried crisp and glazed in a sweet shoyu sauce, pressed onto a block of rice and wrapped with nori. Serves 8 (8 musubi).

ingredients.text: 1 can Spam (340 g), cut into 8 slices
4 sheets nori, cut in half crosswise
ingredients.item: sheets nori, cut in half crosswise

steps.text: Stir 1 tbsp rice vinegar into 900 g hot cooked short-grain rice and keep it covered and warm.
Mix 3 tbsp shoyu (soy sauce), 3 tbsp sugar and 2 tbsp mirin.
Fry 1 can Spam (340 g), cut into 8 slices in a dry nonstick pan over medium-high for 2 minutes per side, until browned and crisp.
Turn the heat to low, pour in the sauce and turn the slices for 1 minute, until the sauce is syrupy and coats the Spam.

Lay a half sheet of 4 sheets nori, cut in half crosswise shiny side down with a musubi mold across its center. Press in about 110 g rice firmly, sprinkle with 2 tbsp furikake (optional), top with a Spam slice and press again.
Push the musubi out of the mold, fold the nori up and over, and seal the end with a grain of rice. Repeat with the rest.

notes:
No mold? Use the empty Spam can, both ends cut off and lined with plastic wrap. Wrapped tightly in plastic, musubi keep at room temperature for the day; don't refrigerate, as the rice hardens.

Popular add-ons: a slice of tamagoyaki between the rice and Spam, or a layer of rice on top too (double-decker).
